title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Spy-Affair Scrutiny (Trump, FBI probe, China chips, NVDA shares)
summary: Gotrade News - Nvidia (NVDA) shares slid more than 4% on Monday, November 9, after its board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a
body_markdown:
The woman, Alice Huang, is a former executive of a Singapore-based Nvidia client and is not related to the CEO; U.S. authorities reportedly concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset, according to[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/trump-says-fbi-investigating-nvidia-ceo-huang-over-chinese-scandal-5014009) . Yahoo Finance identified the client as Megaspeed, which denies diverting chips to China, and cited a New York Times report that the Justice Department is running a criminal inquiry into Megaspeed.


## Jeffries Seeks a Full Nvidia Briefing and China Chip Limits


House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said Congress needs more answers about Nvidia, as reported by Reuters via[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/house-democratic-leader-says-lawmakers-need-answers-on-nvidia-wants-china-chip-restrictions-5013456) . A classified briefing for congressional leaders on Monday briefly discussed Nvidia but mostly focused on Iran, according to Jeffries.


> "We're going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia situation." (Hakeem Jeffries, House Democratic leader, as reported by Reuters)


Jeffries said he "strongly supports" restrictions on U.S. chip sales to China in the final annual defense bill. The Senate's version of that bill would give Congress more authority over AI chip exports to China, press U.S. allies to restrict sales of chipmaking equipment to China and require businesses to track AI chips abroad to combat smuggling, per[Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/house-democratic-leader-says-lawmakers-need-answers-on-nvidia-wants-china-chip-restrictions-5013456) . The U.S. has effectively blocked most advanced chip sales to China since 2022, while Huang has repeatedly urged Washington to allow more sales, according to[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/trump-says-fbi-investigating-nvidia-ceo-huang-over-chinese-scandal-5014009) .


Lawmakers from both parties also weighed in. Democratic Senator Chris Coons called for an investigation to "determine whether our national security was compromised," Investing.com reported, while Republican Representatives Mast, Moolenaar and Crawford asked Huang to appear voluntarily for a closed-door briefing by next week or propose an alternative date by Wednesday, per[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/live/nvidia-scandal-live-updates-nvidia-stock--board-investigates-ceo-jensen-huang-affair-alleged-chinese-spy-163130372.html) . "It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk," the three Republicans wrote.


## Will Huang Stay as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO?


Analysts said it appeared unlikely, for now, that the scandal would lead Huang to step down, according to[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/trump-says-fbi-investigating-nvidia-ceo-huang-over-chinese-scandal-5014009) , which noted governance concerns because Huang, who has led Nvidia since co-founding it in 1993, has few potential successors.


Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy does not expect Huang to be pushed out unless the investigation finds something, as reported by[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/live/nvidia-scandal-live-updates-nvidia-stock--board-investigates-ceo-jensen-huang-affair-alleged-chinese-spy-163130372.html) . Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson said the board's initial statement reduces the chance of an ouster, but that Huang will likely lose some credibility with U.S. government representatives, per the same report.


## AMD and Broadcom (AVGO) Rise With the Market as Nvidia Slides


Nvidia's slide did not spread to its peers on Monday morning. Other chip stocks, including[Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) ,[Broadcom (AVGO)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/avgo/) , Intel, Sandisk and Micron Technology, were unscathed and rose along with broader markets, according to[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/live/nvidia-scandal-live-updates-nvidia-stock--board-investigates-ceo-jensen-huang-affair-alleged-chinese-spy-163130372.html) .


Nvidia's moves still carry weight for the broader market, since the company makes up nearly 7% of the[S&P 500](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/sp-500-what-it-is-and-what-really-moves-it/) , according to Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre.
